title: Traveling now and playing up north
summary: Travels on concert tours and with the Chocolate Music Bars, and racial attitudes up north.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Do you do much traveling now?

Yeah, we have some. We were, well, we were, well, we were, well, we were, You heard what I said about my travel thing I did. Before, 24, I went to Chicago, I was waiting for this track for the steamboat line, and then there's a preservation hall. I know what they expected, and how they carry them, I shall. Now this is a place where I have large work companies, even north of South Dakota went out in that area, with the chalky music bars. And we were, in fact, everywhere we went was sensation, because we knew how to carry ourselves. And there's an Indian reservation out there. Just for curiosity, we went to a truck and then sneaked up some whiskey, but we weren't supposed to have it. And we had some white people who invited us to a place, and some were resented, but it wasn't their business. We all knew how to carry ourselves.

You see? And some places I played up north, had more hatred for the black man than they have in the South. Yeah, and out of the cold, that's right, I want to get you that. It's the sugar beet. Mm-hmm. There was a man with a truck would go pick these people somewhere. I don't know if they went all the way to Mexico, but they were from up in that area. Because a black person probably would do it. It's too down there because they had to be doing this all day long. Oh, yeah. And the Asian, Japanese, Chinese, they could do that, and then South America, some Mexican, they could do that. Excuse me. And we happened to be at the time. I used to go out there and watch and look at them. I'd talk, because I'm talking to the U.S. by now, you see. We found a place for them. They weren't accepted, because it was likely to not accept it up here. But if they need the money, we'd go all over to Mexico to get them, bring them back, and pay them a fairly good price, not the price we'd pay American. No, I had that wrong. Some of them, they did a lot of cheating and everything. But they said we pay them a fair price, and they would go all fine. You could see them with their families and everything, you know, out of the Spanish and things like that. And we happened to be with them at the time. I used to go look at them. And I said, I said, hell, I couldn't do that myself. And I ran her by the Asiatic, the Spanish, some of them were in the South America mixed up with Africa. And the Asian people there, and the Indian, whatever we call our Indian year, and the Spanish. And the Italian do it. I mean, they come up with it, you know. That was another experience.
